newsitem.title: UK: Virgin Cinemas plan big UK investment.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Cinemas plan big UK investment.

text.p: Virgin Cinemas said on Monday that it planned to increase capital investment threefold to 34.5 million stg this year and that it was on track to meet its target of opening 20 new venues over the next three years.
Virgin Cinemas, a consortium headed by Richard Branson's Virgin Group, reported a 90 percent increase in net operating profits to 13.5 million stg in 1996 from seven million the previous year.

Virgin Cinemas was set up following the purchase of the UK MGM chain in July 1995 from Credit Lyonnais for some 200 million stg. It sold off 90 traditional cinemas to a management buy-in at the ABC group last May, leaving it with 26 multiplex sites across the UK.

The company has subsequently opened new multiplexes in the southern town of Rochester and Wigan in north-west England. It plans to open new venues this year in Aberdeen in Scotland, Newport in Wales and Boldon, north-east England.
The increased investment will help to refurbish existing cinemas and fund the expansion.
"Today's announcement illustrates that our strategy of concentrating growth in the larger multiplex sites is proving highly successful," said Simon Burke, chairman of Virgin Cinemas.
"Our investment programme for the next two years will ensure Virgin Cinemas' rapid growth and secure some of the best new cinema sites in the UK," he added.
Cinema attendance in the UK has recovered strongly since the advent of the multiplex in the mid 1980s. Annual attendance is now running at around 125 million, up from around 50 million a decade ago.
Virgin's partners in the cinema chain are Texas Pacific Group, Colony Capital and Hotel Property Group.
